newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish parliament to vote on Ciller charges.
newsitem.headline: Turkish parliament to vote on Ciller charges.

text.p: Turkish MPs are to vote on Tuesday on whether to send Tansu Ciller, the deputy prime minister, to the Supreme Court on two corruption charges dating from her three-year spell as premier, parliament officials said.

A parliamentary session beginning at 3 p.m. (1300 GMT) will hear accusations that Ciller abused her power to influence the sale of state-owned carmaker TOFAS and failed to prevent corruption at the TEDAS electricity company.
Two separate votes were expected later in the day. The Islamist-led coalition would be in deep trouble if Ciller lost the votes but analysts predict a narrow victory for her.
The opposition is six short of the 276 deputies needed to impeach Ciller and must rely on defections from among her True Path Party or Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party.
Conservative Ciller became Turkey's first woman leader in 1993 but ceded the premiership to Erbakan last year after losing general elections to Welfare in 1995.
She faces a further corruption vote, on the source of her substantial personal wealth, in parliament on Wednesday. The government must also deal with an opposition censure motion next week.
